summary: 16-bit pixel fill with a per-pixel stride step plus a Bresenham-style conditional scanline advance: stores a fixed 16-bit value, advances the pointer by a small byte step a8 on every pixel, and adds a larger row byte stride whenever the error accumulator crosses zero. No calls, no globals.

operations.description: Compute the starting pixel pointer: buffer base address a9 plus twice the pixel offset a6, where twice the offset accounts for two bytes per 16-bit pixel.
Compute the conditional row byte stride as twice a5, converting the pixel-unit row stride a5 into a byte stride for 16-bit pixels.
Compute the per-pixel byte stride as twice a8, converting the pixel-unit step a8 into a byte step for 16-bit pixels.
Record the fill value a7 as the value that will be stored into each pixel and returned.
Iterate exactly a2 times, decrementing a2 each pass and stopping when it reaches zero.
Store the 16-bit fill value a7 at the current pixel pointer, then advance the pointer forward by the per-pixel byte stride.
If the error accumulator a1 is negative, add a3 to it (stay on the current scanline). Otherwise add a4 and additionally advance the pointer by the conditional row byte stride.

unresolved: The per-pixel stride a8 suggests a sloped or diagonal line fill, but the exact geometric primitive is unconfirmed without caller evidence.
Parameter roles for a3 vs. a4 are inferred from the two error-accumulator branches; no caller or header evidence confirms which is the major-axis increment.
